prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the project's two Umbraco MCP servers, umbraco and umbraco-editor.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP servers won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP servers.

Always use the MCP servers to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Everything is verified and the site is running. Final report:

## What I built

**A blog site ("MCP Matters") — modeled, filled, and rendered entirely through the two MCP servers, following AGENTS.md/UMBRACO-RULES.md.**

**Content modeling (umbraco server)**
- `Blog Block Grid` data type (12 columns, inline create) with 6 blocks + shared `BlockSettings` (color picker, spacing, anchor): `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `headingBlock`, `quoteBlock`, `postListBlock`
- Page types `blogFrontPage` + `blogPost` (excerpt + blocks) in `Pages/`, element types moved into `Blocks/`, templates assigned, `blogPost` allowed under the front page
- Templates `siteLayout`, `blogFrontPage`, `blogPost`
- Media: 4 Unsplash photos imported into a `Blog` folder (rule 8); color palette added to the shipped "Approved Color" picker (values are stored **without** `#` in v18)
- Two config bumps required: `siteRoot` had to allow `blogFrontPage` as a child, and the **WWW node was left without a domain** — `/` + `en-US` went on the front page per rule 9

**Content (umbraco-editor server)**
- Front page: hero (bg image + CTA), post-list block, rich text, pull quote
- **"Why MCP is awesome"** — 9 blocks (hero, copy, heading, 3 two-column reasons, image w/ caption, quote, closer)
- **"MCP + Umbraco: better together"** — 5 blocks, incl. an image block exercising `blockSettings` (background color + 24px spacing)

**Razor (after the modeled-DB rebuild, per the AGENTS.md order)**
- Umbraco's pipeline untouched: `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync` → `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` adapters (pure `BlockGridItem<T>` in, view-model out) → `ViewComponent`s in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/` holding all markup. Plain records live in `Models/Blocks/` (no loose files in `Models/` root); Tailwind classes in the views; `npm run build` produced `wwwroot/dist/`.

## How to view it

Site is running now (`dotnet run` in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco`, background task): **https://localhost:44317/**
- `/` — front page listing both posts
- `/why-mcp-is-awesome/` and `/mcp-plus-umbraco-better-together/` (that's the URL Umbraco generated for the `+` in the title)

## What isn't working / caveats

- **Publishing needed a detour**: `publish-page` with `includeDescendants` requires an interactive MCP confirmation that auto-cancelled in this autonomous run (tried both publish paths). Publishing pages **individually** went through — everything is live.
- One leftover **empty heading block** on the front page: my duplicate heading is blanked (renders nothing) but couldn't be deleted — `delete-block` prompts were cancelled. Cosmetic, visible only in the backoffice.
- Image URLs are signed via `GetCropUrl()` (verified 200); a hand-written query string would 400 as AGENTS.md warns.
- uSync exports are on disk (`ContentTypes/`, `DataTypes/`, `Media/`, `Templates/`) per rule 10; no migrations were written — all schema went through MCP.
